subsystems.name: Exciton medium
subsystems.role: provides the bound electron-hole pairs that supply optical gain and nonlinearity.
parts: quantum wells or a perovskite/organic layer

subsystems.name: Optical microcavity
subsystems.role: traps light long enough that it stops behaving as a free photon and couples strongly to the excitons.

subsystems.name: Excitation
subsystems.role: pumps energy in to create excitons.
parts: or electrical contacts for injected carriers

subsystems.name: Tuning and control
subsystems.role: sets the energy match between photon mode and exciton, which decides how polariton-like the state is.

subsystems.name: Readout
subsystems.role: measures the hybrid state and, in a device, extracts light.

buildSteps.title: Grow the heterostructure
buildSteps.detail: Molecular-beam or metal-organic vapour deposition builds layers a few nanometres thick, with the quantum wells placed exactly at the antinode of the light field.

buildSteps.title: Make the mirrors
buildSteps.detail: Alternating layers of two semiconductors of different refractive index are stacked dozens of times to reflect over 99% of the light.

buildSteps.title: Form the cavity
buildSteps.detail: The spacer between the mirrors is etched into mesas, pillars or waveguides so that light is confined in all three dimensions.

buildSteps.title: Tune the resonance
buildSteps.detail: Temperature or angle is adjusted so the cavity photon energy sits close to the exciton energy — the condition for strong coupling.

buildSteps.title: Confirm strong coupling
buildSteps.detail: The spectrum splits into two peaks separated by the Rabi splitting instead of a single cavity mode; this is the signature of polaritons, not separate light and matter.

buildSteps.title: Reach condensation
buildSteps.detail: Above a threshold pump power the polaritons crowd into one quantum state, forming a condensate that emits coherently — often at higher temperature than an equivalent conventional laser.

buildSteps.title: Build a device
buildSteps.detail: Contacts, waveguides, interferometers or arrays of coupled pillars are added to make switches, transistors or lattices.

buildSteps.title: Scale to arrays
buildSteps.detail: Many coupled condensates are wired or optically addressed together to act as a simulator or a logic network.

prerequisites.why: strong coupling needs excitons that survive long enough to exchange energy with the light field.
the photon must bounce thousands of times to build the coupling strength.
achieved in wide-bandgap and organic or perovskite materials; older gallium-arsenide devices must be cooled to a few kelvin.
most demonstrations are optically pumped with a laser, which no useful chip can rely on.
a computing or simulation system needs many devices connected without the light leaking away.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations of polariton condensation, polariton lasing and all-optical switching
pathway.unlocks: proof that hybrid light-matter states can carry and process signals.

pathway.milestone: room-temperature devices driven by electric current rather than a pump laser
pathway.unlocks: a route from optics bench to chip.

pathway.milestone: coupled arrays used as analogue simulators for optimisation and lattice problems
pathway.unlocks: special-purpose computing where polaritons solve problems a digital chip finds hard.

pathway.milestone: integrated polariton logic operating at very low switching energy
pathway.unlocks: optical computing blocks that sit alongside conventional photonics, if losses and fabrication yield can be mastered.
